body.en: At about ten or eleven, Douglas decided to learn to swim. The *YMCA pool* in Yakima seemed safe because it was only two or three feet deep at the shallow end and about nine feet at the deep end. He began cautiously, using water wings and paddling in the shallow end, still uneasy.

points.en: Shallow end two to three feet, deep end about nine feet
He used water wings and stayed careful
He was still afraid of water

body.en: One day, while he sat alone at the edge of the pool, a big older boy picked him up and tossed him into the deep end. Douglas planned to spring up from the bottom when his feet touched it, but each time he came up slowly and too weakly. He went down again and again, gripped by panic. At last the terror gave way to a strange calm, and he lost consciousness. He woke up lying beside the pool, sick and shaken.

problem.en: Describe Douglas's experience in the YMCA pool and its effect on him.

steps.en: Set the scene: the YMCA pool in Yakima; shallow and deep ends.
Narrate the accident: thrown in by an older boy; his plan to spring up.
Describe the struggle: rising slowly, sinking again, panic, then blackout.
Give the effect: a deep, lasting fear that spoiled water activities for years.

answer.en: Thrown into the deep end by an older boy, Douglas nearly drowned despite trying to spring up from the bottom. The experience left him with a deep terror of water that haunted him for years.
